title: Diversity of pathogenicity among rice blast fungus (Pyricularia oryzae) isolates in Bangladesh
authors: Kabir, M. S.; Mian, M. S.; Akter, S.; Latif, M. A.
key_findings: Identified 18 distinct pathotypes among 75 Pyricularia oryzae isolates collected across Bangladesh. Documented high virulence on widely grown mega-varieties BRRI dhan28 and BRRI dhan29 during Boro season.

title: Cross Infection between Rice and Wheat Blast Pathogen Pyricularia oryzae in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.; Rahman, M. M.
key_findings: Demonstrated that Magnaporthe oryzae isolates from infected wheat heads can cause mild lesions on vulnerable rice seedlings under humid greenhouse conditions, though host specialization between MoT and MoO lineages is maintained.

title: Management of Rice Blast (Magnaporthe Oryzae B. Couch) Using Bioagents and Fungicides in Bangladesh
authors: Sultana, R.; Mia, M. A. T.; Latif, M. A.; Islam, M. R.
key_findings: Evaluated Trichoderma harzianum and commercial fungicides; Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.75 g/L and Kasugamycin at 2 mL/L provided 82% and 76% blast suppression respectively under field conditions.

title: Antifungal potential of commercial silver nanoparticles against rice blast pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae in Bangladesh
authors: Akter, N.; Islam, M. T.; Rahman, M. A.
key_findings: Demonstrated that silver nanoparticles (30-50 nm) at 50 ppm achieved complete inhibition of conidial germination and appressorium formation in P. oryzae.

title: Strategy for Rice Disease Management in Bangladesh
authors: Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Kabir, M. S.
key_findings: Comprehensive disease survey across 30 AEZs: blast and sheath blight represent 65% of all chemical fungicide interventions; highlights critical early warning need based on canopy humidity >90% and night temperatures 20-24°C.

disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
title: Genetic Divergence of Rice Genotypes Revealed by Bacterial Blight Disease and SSR Markers in Bangladesh
authors: Akter, S.; Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Islam, M. R.
key_findings: Screened 45 rice germplasm lines against Xoo isolates; identified functional resistance alleles Xa4 and Xa21; recommended marker-assisted introgressions into modern Boro varieties.

disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
title: Molecular marker assisted gene stacking for multiple diseases resistance in rice in Bangladesh
authors: Hasan, M. M.; Rafii, M. Y.; Latif, M. A.; Rahim, H. A.
key_findings: Pyramided Xa21 and xa13 bacterial blight resistance genes with blast resistance genes Pi2/Pi9, achieving broad-spectrum resistance against virulent Bangladeshi strains.

disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
title: Identification of Rice Germplasm with Resistance to Bacterial Leaf Blight in Bangladesh
authors: Latif, M. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Mia, M. A. T.
key_findings: Screened 120 Bangladeshi and IRRI rice lines against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae; identified high resistance in BRRI dhan31 and DV85 carrying Xa5 and Xa7 genes.

title: Biological Control of Rice Sheath Blight Disease (Rhizoctonia solani) Using Antagonistic Bacteria in Bangladesh
authors: Mitu, S. A.; Latif, M. A.; Mia, M. A. T.; Akter, S.
key_findings: Isolated indigenous Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens strains from rice rhizosphere; achieved 68.4% reduction in sheath blight lesion height and sustained grain weight under field microplot trials.

title: Standardization of inoculation techniques for sheath blight of rice in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. R.
key_findings: Established that micro-chamber Typha-strip inoculation at maximum tillering under relative humidity >90% yields uniform sheath blight infection for resistance screening.

title: Epidemiology and management of false smut of rice (Ustilaginoidea virens) in Bangladesh
authors: Latif, M. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Mia, M. A. T.
key_findings: Documented rising incidence of false smut in hybrid and high-yielding Boro varieties receiving excessive nitrogenous fertilizers (>120 kg N/ha); yield losses reach 15-25% via smut ball formation.

title: Historical Milestones and Genomic Evolution in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae Research
authors: Midha, S.; Patil, P. B.; Swings, J.
key_findings: Traces pathotype evolution of Xoo in tropical rice systems; TAL effector diversity drives susceptibility in traditional landraces.

title: Transmission biology and vector dynamics of Rice Tungro Bacilliform and Spherical Viruses in Bangladesh
authors: Kabir, M. S.; Latif, M. A.; Ali, M. A.
key_findings: Nephotettix virescens green leafhopper populations surge following late monsoon rains; synchronized planting and light traps reduce vector numbers and tungro stunting incidence by over 70%.

title: Screening of Rice Genotypes for Resistance to Blast (Pyricularia oryzae) under Subtropical Climates
authors: Akter, S.; Mian, M. S.; Latif, M. A.
key_findings: Field screening identified differential blast reaction between seedling leaf blast and reproductive neck blast; validated resistant alleles in BRRI dhan65.

title: Morphological and Molecular Characterization of Pyricularia oryzae Isolates Causing Rice Blast
authors: Wahyudi, T.; Prasetyo, J.; Maryono, T.
key_findings: Demonstrates sporulation optima between 24-26°C with 100% relative humidity; appressoria melanization inhibited by tricyclazole.

title: Head Rice Recovery, Comparative Advantage, and Disease Loss Dynamics in Bangladesh
authors: Kabir, M. S.; Rahman, M. C.; Salam, M. A.
key_findings: Quantified post-harvest milling losses attributed to fungal panicle glume discoloration and neck blast; grain breakage rises by 35% in blast-affected lots.

title: Mating types of Fusarium fujikuroi from bakanae disease of rice in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. M.; Bashar, M. A.; Sultana, R.
key_findings: Identified both MAT-1 and MAT-2 mating types among Bangladeshi bakanae isolates; demonstrated seed-treatment with carbendazim or fludioxonil provides 90%+ control of seedling elongation.

title: Advancing Salinity-Tolerant Rice in Bangladesh: The Case of BRRI dhan67 and Disease Dynamics
authors: Kabir, M. S.; Salam, M. A.; Islam, M. R.
key_findings: Assessed disease reaction of BRRI dhan67 across variable salinities; high ambient humidity in microclimates overrides salinity-induced leaf wax thickening to allow localized blast outbreaks.

title: Assessing the Adoption and Adoption Gap of Selected BRRI Released Boro Rice Varieties in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Rahman, M. C.
key_findings: Farmers report disease susceptibility (primarily neck blast and sheath blight) as the single primary reason for replacing older cultivars BRRI dhan28 and BRRI dhan29 with newer resistant varieties BRRI dhan89 and BRRI dhan92.

title: Assessment of Genetic Diversity in Bangladeshi Rice Blast Pathogen Populations
authors: Sultana, R.; Mia, M. A. T.; Latif, M. A.
journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Exploring Engineering
key_findings: Field surveillance and engineering analysis: light trap catches of pest vectors and dew sensors predict spore release peaks in Boro seedbeds.

title: Emergence of wheat blast in Bangladesh was caused by a South American lineage of Magnaporthe oryzae
authors: Islam, M. T.; Croll, D.; Gladieux, P.; Soanes, D. M. et al.
key_findings: Definitive peer-reviewed publication confirming emergence of South American MoT lineage in southwestern Bangladesh with 100% field yield loss on legacy cultivars.

title: Wheat Blast: A New Fungal Inhabitant to Bangladesh Threatening World Wheat Production
authors: Malaker, P. K.; Barma, N. C. D.; Tiwari, T. P.; Collis, W. J. et al.
key_findings: Comprehensive epidemiological review: over 15,000 hectares affected in 2016 with yield losses up to 100%; documents symptom progression from bleached spikes to shriveled grain.

title: Economic benefits of blast-resistant biofortified wheat in Bangladesh: The case of BARI Gom 33
authors: Mottaleb, K. A.; Singh, P. K.; Sonderman, C. A.; Kruseman, G.
key_findings: Adoption of 2NS-translocation carrying blast-resistant biofortified variety BARI Gom 33 delivers substantial national economic return, mitigating annual risk of $13 million in crop failure.

title: Wheat blast disease: Bangladesh and global perspectives of blast resistance
authors: Hossain, M. M.; Meah, M. B.; Kabir, M. S.
journal_or_publisher: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
key_findings: Identified high vulnerability in legacy cultivars (Prodip, BARI Gom 26); confirmed resistance in BARI Gom 33 and WMRI breeding lines carrying the Aegilops ventricosa 2NS translocation segment.

title: Effects of plant extracts on controlling wheat blast disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum pathotype in Bangladesh
authors: Mahbub, M. S.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
key_findings: Evaluated botanicals against MoT conidia; allicin-rich garlic extract and ginger rhizome extracts inhibited spore germination by 78% in in-vitro and spikelet assays.

title: Oligomycins inhibit Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum and suppress wheat blast in Bangladesh
authors: Chakraborty, M.; Mahmud, N. U.; Gupta, D. R.; Islam, M. T.
geographic_scope: Bangladesh (Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Agricultural University, Gazipur)
key_findings: Discovered that natural oligomycins from marine Streptomyces completely halt conidial germination and appressorium differentiation of Bangladeshi MoT isolates.

title: Host Resistance to Spot Blotch (Bipolaris Sorokiniana) in Wheat across South Asia and Bangladesh
authors: Duveiller, E.; Sharma, R. C.; Joshi, A. K.
journal_or_publisher: Management of Wheat and Barley Diseases
key_findings: Documents Bipolaris sorokiniana spot blotch as the primary biotic constraint to wheat in the warm, humid plains of Bangladesh; yield reductions average 18-35% in susceptible genotypes.

title: Effect of wheat cultivar mixtures on spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana) severity and yield in Bangladesh
authors: Malaker, P. K.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
key_findings: Pioneering field experimentation demonstrating that cultivar mixtures of resistant and moderately susceptible lines reduced area under disease progress curve (AUDPC) by 28%.

title: Phylogeographic population diversity of Bipolaris sorokiniana causing spot blotch of wheat in South Asia
authors: Aggarwal, R.; Gurjar, M. S.; Bashyal, B. M.
key_findings: Genomic profiling shows high gene flow across Bangladesh and Eastern India wheat regions; pathotype 1-2 predominantly virulent on traditional varieties.

title: Mitigating the twin problems of malnutrition and wheat blast by one wheat variety in Bangladesh: The Case of BARI Gom 33
authors: Mottaleb, K. A.; Govindan, V.; Singh, P. K.; Sonder, K.
key_findings: Detailed agronomic and biofortification study: BARI Gom 33 confers complete blast resistance via 2NS translocation while providing 51 mg/kg grain zinc.

title: Variability of Bipolaris maydis in relation to maydis blight severity in maize
authors: Singh, V.; Sharma, S.; Kumar, P.; Hooda, K. S.
key_findings: Analyzed thermal and moisture response of 32 Bipolaris maydis isolates; optimum radial mycelial growth occurs at 28-30°C and 90% RH; conidial germination drops below 18°C.

title: Management of Maydis Leaf Blight Disease of Maize Caused by Bipolaris maydis Using Biocontrol Agents and Fungicides
authors: Devi, S.; Lal, A. A.; Simon, S.
journal_or_publisher: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
key_findings: Foliar application of Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC at 1 mL/L demonstrated 74.8% disease reduction and 26.5% yield increase over untreated check.

title: Morphological and Molecular Variation of Isolates Causing Maydis Leaf Blight in Subtropical Maize
authors: Yadav, O. P.; Hossain, F.; Karjagi, C. G.
key_findings: Characterized teleomorph Cochliobolus heterostrophus; Race T susceptibility confirmed in male sterile cytoplasm lines; Race O predominant across northern plains.

disease: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii)
title: Influence of Weather Parameters on Development of Maydis Leaf Blight in Maize
authors: Kumar, A.; Singh, V.; Hooda, K. S.
journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
key_findings: Correlated Maydis leaf blight progress with relative humidity >85% and maximum temperatures between 28-32°C; disease severity increased by 14% per day during persistent cloudiness.

disease: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii)
title: Rhizosphere Trichoderma isolates as potential biocontrol agent for Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight of Maize
authors: Gautam, A.; Sharma, S.; Kumar, R.
journal_or_publisher: Proceedings of the Indian National Science Academy
key_findings: Trichoderma asperellum effectively parasitized R. solani sclerotia in maize field soils, reducing seedling damping-off and basal sheath blight incidence by 58%.

title: QTLs Mapping for Turcicum Leaf Blight Resistance in Maize (Zea Mays L.)
authors: Rahman, M. M.; Ali, M. L.; Islam, M. R.
key_findings: Identified major genomic QTLs on chromosome 2 and 5 imparting field tolerance against Exserohilum turcicum in BARI hybrid maize lines.

title: Assessment of genetics for turcicum leaf blight resistance in maize (Zea mays L.) in Bangladesh
authors: Rahman, M. M.; Islam, M. S.; Amiruzzaman, M.
key_findings: Demonstrated additive gene action governing Ht1/Ht2 resistance genes against northern corn leaf blight; recommends winter sowing timing to escape humid sporulation peaks.

title: Variability and traits association in maize (Zea mays L.) for yield and foliar health in Bangladesh
authors: Amiruzzaman, M.; Islam, M. A.; Hassan, L.
journal_or_publisher: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
key_findings: Evaluated 24 BARI hybrid maize genotypes; BARI Hybrid Maize-9 and BARI Hybrid Maize-7 exhibited minimal foliar blight progression and superior harvest index under Barind conditions.

title: Efficacy of selected fungicides and antibacterial chemicals against Fusarium stalk rot in maize
authors: Sharma, P.; Kumar, A.; Hooda, K. S.
key_findings: Post-flowering water stress and lodging predispose stalks to vascular occlusion by Fusarium verticillioides; balanced potassium and soil drench with carbendazim suppress vascular breakdown.

title: Responses of TIBA on growth, yield and disease tolerance components of BARI Maize in Bangladesh
authors: Sultana, N.; Rahman, M. M.; Hossain, M. A.
journal_or_publisher: Journal of Bangladesh Academy of Sciences
key_findings: Canopy architecture modification via anti-auxin treatments enhanced lower canopy air circulation, significantly reducing microclimatic humidity and sheath blight progression.

title: Ralstonia solanacearum: A Threat to Potato Production in Bangladesh
authors: Miah, M. N. A.; Rahman, M. M.; Hossain, M. M.
key_findings: Landmark Bangladesh study replacing erroneous prior citation: documents Ralstonia solanacearum race 3 biovar 2 as dominant pathogen causing up to 45% vascular tuber rot in northern Bangladesh; proves disease occurs primarily when warm soil temperatures (>28°C) coincide with excess soil moisture/waterlogging, with zero foliar leaf wetness requirement.

title: Profitability and Disease Reaction of BARI Released Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) Varieties in Bangladesh
authors: Sarker, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.
key_findings: Evaluated Diamant, Cardinal, BARI Alu-7, and BARI Alu-8; documented late blight and bacterial wilt loss differentials; verified benefit-cost ratio of 1.82 with timely preventative fungicidal sprays.

title: Canopy Reflectance Measurements Used to Estimate Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) Severity in Potato
authors: Popescu, S.; Donescu, V.; Ilie, M.
key_findings: Demonstrates that multispectral vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, and red edge position) reliably capture foliar late blight destruction 4-6 days before visible chlorosis expands.

title: Impact of potato var. BARI Alu-25 adoption on the growers’ livelihood and disease incidence in Bangladesh
authors: Rashid, M. A.; Islam, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.
key_findings: Adoption of moderately late-blight resistant cultivar BARI Alu-25 reduced necessary fungicide applications from 7-9 sprays per season to 2-3 sprays, raising farmer net income by 34%.

title: Adoption and profitability of BARI released potato varieties in northern region of Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. S.; Miah, M. A. M.; Rashid, M. A.
key_findings: Evaluated Diamant, Cardinal, BARI Alu-7, and BARI Alu-25 across 300 commercial farms; shows that disease-free certified foundation seed tubers eliminate 80% of primary bacterial wilt and PLRV infections.

title: Screening of Exotic and Local Potato Germplasm against Potato Virus PVX, PVY and PLRV
authors: Khan, M. A.; Rashid, A.; Ahmad, I.
key_findings: Myzus persicae aphid vectors transmit Potato Leaf Roll Virus (PLRV) and PVY during mid-season warming (January-February); roguing infected seed potatoes within 4 weeks after emergence prevents field degeneration.

title: Tomato leaf curl Patna virus causing tomato leaf curl disease in Bangladesh
authors: Roy, B.; Islam, M. S.; Akhter, S.; Malaker, P. K.
key_findings: Confirmed molecular identity of Begomovirus causing up to 85% yield reduction in commercial tomato fields in Bangladesh; identified transmission exclusively through sweetpotato whitefly Bemisia tabaci.

title: Association of tomato leaf curl Gujarat virus and tomato leaf curl Bangladesh virus with tomato leaf curl disease in Bangladesh
authors: Sultana, R.; Islam, M. T.; Brown, J. K.
key_findings: Revealed mixed begomovirus infections and betasatellite complexes driving aggressive curling, stunting, and flower abortion; validates vector control with yellow sticky traps and systemic neonicotinoid seedlings drenches.

disease: Bacterial Wilt & Soil-Borne Disease in Tomato
title: Combination of biological control agents and garlic (Allium sativum) extract against bacterial and fungal wilt of tomato in Bangladesh
authors: Islam, M. R.; Akter, N.; Hossain, M. M.
key_findings: Combined soil application of Trichoderma harzianum and aqueous garlic clove extract (1:10) suppressed bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum) and Fusarium oxysporum incidence by 62% in summer tomato plots.

title: Tomato Cultivation in Bangladesh: Insights into Pest Awareness and Disease Management
authors: Hossain, M. S.; Mian, M. A. H.; Rahman, M. M.
journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Agriculture and Biology
key_findings: Surveys farm-level disease occurrence: Early blight (Alternaria solani) and Late blight (P. infestans) are primary foliar bottlenecks in winter tomatoes; Difenoconazole (0.05%) and Mancozeb (0.2%) remain standard DAE treatments.

title: Bio-rational management for root-knot and wilt disease complex of tomato in Bangladesh
authors: Rahman, M. A.; Ahmad, M. U.; Hossain, I.
key_findings: Meloidogyne incognita wounding exacerbates Ralstonia solanacearum ingress; mustard oilcake (300 kg/ha) and Paecilomyces lilacinus soil amendment suppressed root galling and vascular wilt simultaneously.

title: Progressive impact of alternaria blight on antioxidants enzyme of mustard (Brassica campestris L.) in Bangladesh
authors: Sarker, B. C.; Roy, B.; Hasan, M. M.
key_findings: Shows Alternaria brassicae infection severely reduces catalase and superoxide dismutase activity, leading to premature pod shattering and 32-55% seed yield deficit in Tori-7 and BARI Sarisha-14 under heavy dew conditions.

title: Studies on management of Alternaria blight (Alternaria brassicae) of mustard through fungicides and bio-agents
authors: Choudhary, R.; Singh, S. K.; Kumar, A.
key_findings: Foliar spray of Iprodione 50 WP (Rovral @ 2 g/L) at 45 and 60 days after sowing achieved 76.4% disease control and maximized 1000-seed weight and oil content.

title: Harnessing Hypovirulence: Mycovirus-induced modulation of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum on Brassica crops
authors: Sharma, P.; Kumar, V.; Rai, P. K.
journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Agricultural and Plant Science
key_findings: Sclerotinia stem rot emerges in high-fertility winter mustard when canopy closes; sclerotia carpogenically germinate under moist soil and temperatures 15-20°C, releasing airborne ascospores infecting senescent petals.

title: Efficacy of fungicides to control Stemphylium blight (Stemphylium botryosum) in lentil in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. S.; Bakr, M. A.; Dey, T. K.
key_findings: Pioneering BARI research establishing Rovral 50 WP (Iprodione @ 2 g/L) and Secure 600 WG (Fenamidone + Mancozeb @ 1.5 g/L) as most effective fungicides, reducing Stemphylium leaf blighting by 71% and lifting seed yield by 45%.

title: Epidemiology of Stemphylium Blight of Lentil in Bangladesh
authors: Bakr, M. A.; Ahmed, H. U.; Rahman, M. M.
journal_or_publisher: Bangladesh Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research
key_findings: Quantified weather triggers: night temperature 18-22°C, relative humidity >85%, and dense canopy morning dew duration >6 hours promote explosive conidiophore proliferation in February.

title: Race identification in Uromyces vicia-fabae causing lentil rust and host response
authors: Kumar, S.; Saxena, D. R.; Basandrai, A. K.
key_findings: Delineated virulent pathotypes across sub-Himalayan lentil tracts; verified high resistance in BARI Masur-6 and BARI Masur-8 against prevalent teliospore populations.

title: Chili anthracnose: Colletotrichum species complex, biology, and management
authors: Saxena, A.; Raghuwanshi, R.; Gupta, V. K.; Singh, H. B.
geographic_scope: South Asia / Tropical chili growing regions
key_findings: Documents Colletotrichum capsici and C. gloeosporioides as primary causal agents of fruit rot and dieback; splash dispersal occurs during warm rainy intervals (27-30°C, RH >80%); recommended spray program with azoxystrobin and copper oxychloride.

title: Forecasting Anthracnose (Colletotrichum capsici) Attack on Chili Using Microclimate Correlation
authors: Widiastuti, A.; Suryanti, S.; Ningrum, P.
key_findings: Mathematical correlation models confirm fruit rot incidence spikes when rain events coincide with temperatures >26°C and surface fruit wetness >5 hours.

title: Eco-friendly Management of Purple Blotch (Alternaria Porri (Ellis) Cif.) of Onion (Allium Cepa L.) in Bangladesh
authors: Hossain, M. I.; Meah, M. B.; Islam, M. T.
key_findings: Direct Bangladesh field trial: Trichoderma harzianum bio-agent and garlic bulb extract combined with Mancozeb (Dithane M-45 @ 0.2%) provided 73.5% reduction in purple blotch leaf lesions and boosted bulb yield by 31.8%.
